story: Gary is bench-testing a light strip circuit in his garage, with nothing going on the golf cart until the HOA approves it. Donna is checking her club calendar, where court one with Gary and a cobbler for Rosa's five o'clock dinner are both penciled in. Hal is reviewing his violation notebook to make sure nothing is pending, and he jots down a reminder about Rosa's cornbread. Rosa, hopeful about the evening, is laying out the long table and planning seats so the neighbors end up sitting together.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Wire and bench-test the light strip circuit indoors, nothing mounted to the cart until approval
Donna (donna club calendar): Check today's schedule: court one with Gary this afternoon, cobbler and ice cream for Rosa's at five
Hal (hal violation notebook): Review the notebook, confirm nothing is pending, and jot down a reminder for Rosa's dinner: cornbread, table, on time
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out the long table, lay the cloth, and plan the seating so the neighbors sit together

gary.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM Saturday, I'm home alone. The application is filed, but L-01 says exterior cart mods need Architectural Review approval, and I only filed, I haven't been approved. So no installing anything visible on the cart yet. The bench work is legal and indoors. L-03 quiet hours end at 7 AM, but I'll keep it quiet anyway, nothing amplified until approved. Court with Donna is this afternoon and dinner at Rosa's at five, so I have a free morning. Best use is to keep tinkering at the workbench: wire up the lighting circuit and test it on the bench, no street visibility, no sound.

parameters.content: Wire and bench-test the light strip circuit indoors, nothing mounted to the cart until approval

donna.thought_process: It's Saturday morning, the day of Rosa's dinner at five. I'm at home with the calendar, my pickleball bag, and my phone. I've got court one in the afternoon with Gary, then the walk over to Rosa's with the ice cream and cobbler. Nobody's around to talk to, so the best use of this hour is to check my club calendar and make sure the day is laid out: court time (staying within the 2-hour limit), cobbler prep, and ice cream pickup.

parameters.content: Check today's schedule: court one with Gary this afternoon, cobbler and ice cream for Rosa's at five

hal.thought_process: Saturday morning, 7:17 AM, and the street is quiet. The notebook has Gary and Donna marked resolved, and the notices are cleared. Tonight is Rosa's dinner and I owe her an on-time arrival with the cornbread, after missing the table last time. No one is around, so no sense chasing anyone. Best use of the hour is to check the notebook and make sure nothing is pending, then plan the day around getting the cornbread and the table carried in without a fuss.

parameters.content: Review the notebook, confirm nothing is pending, and jot down a reminder for Rosa's dinner: cornbread, table, on time

rosa.thought_process: It's Saturday morning, 7:17 AM, and the welcome dinner is tonight at five. Hal has the cornbread, Donna the cobbler, Gary the ice and chairs. What's left is mine: the long table and the main dish. I'm home alone, with the dining table and kitchen right here. I've already said my goodbyes to the neighbors, so no need to chase anyone. Best use of this hour is to get the dining table set up and start thinking through the seating so Hal, Gary, and Donna end up side by side.

parameters.content: Set out the long table, lay the cloth, and plan the seating so the neighbors sit together

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
